# Learnings and mistakes

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
MISTAKE, correction class, and the stated reason this session scored 3 of 5.
An input package was assembled for the BrotherSBE refocus stream without first
reading the plan it was meant to feed. It re-derived ratified decisions (the
six-tax model, archetypes D and G, items A1 to A4) and carried five stale facts:
PR 38 open when it had been merged, cut version 1.0.0 when 3.0.0 is ratified,
build a one-pager that exists as tools/sbe_onepager.py, build reporting mode
that exists as tools/sbe_report.py, and do not touch a branch that was already
deleted. Corrected by adding 06-DELTA-AGAINST-THE-V3-PLAN.md rather than by
quietly rewriting the package. Same defect class the product exists to catch:
confident output over material never examined.

MISTAKE. Scored 1 of 5 earlier for producing adoption strategy when the founder
needed practical workflow guidance. Root cause: optimised for convincing people
rather than for using the thing. Fixed by running the tool against a realistic
change, which produced more usable findings in five minutes than the preceding
strategy work did in hours.

NEAR MISS. A zero-file diff was first reported to the founder as a defect. It is
not: the test repository had a single branch, so the merge base with the default
branch was the commit itself and zero files was correct. Caught and re-scoped
before it reached a build stream, which would have sent someone to fix working
code.

LEARNING. Running the product beats reading its documentation for finding
adoption blockers. Both new findings came from execution; neither is visible in
any document.

LEARNING, mechanical. `grep ... | head && echo CLEAN` always reports clean,
because a pipeline's exit status is the last command's and head always exits 0.
Two safety scans in this session were wrong until rewritten to capture output
into a variable and test it.
